To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the port competitiveness is the result of the joint effort of port stakeholders to satisfy the needs of their clients, through the exploitation and integration of resources, in the satisfaction of the needs of the port clients.
the competitiveness of a port is determined by the ability to generate value through the exploitation of interdependencies between port actors in a supply chain.

1) port competitiveness is based on the development of interdependencies between port actors in order to satisfy clients' needs; 2) Port Authority has a key role in identifying those critical assets that encourage the development of port actors interdependencies; and 3) the definition of port critical assets is a key factor in port competitiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of key factors in port value constellation that can be exploited by the Port Authority to improve port competitiveness.
the identification of critical assets and inter-organisatio nal relationships in port competitiveness.
identifying those activities, resources and interdependencies that are crucial for the development of a pro-active role of ports in the new competitive environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the competitiveness of ports is based on the ability to create and manage the critical assets, that are the resources that enable the port to generate value in the supply chain through the interdependencies between port actors.
port competitiveness is a function of the activities, resources and interorganisational relationships developed in the port.

port competitiveness is the result of an integrated approach to port management that involves all the port actors, through the development of a pro-active and value oriented strategy, based on the exploitation of the critical assets of the port.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the port competitiveness is not only determined by the port actors but also by the relationships between the port actors.

port actors are able to generate competitive advantages only through the integration of their activities and resources, but such integration can be effective only if it is based on a common vision, that is the result of the Port Authority's effort to create and manage a shared value system among port actors.
the Port Authority should play the role of a catalyst of value creation for its customers and for the port itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the port competitiveness is not only the result of the port's capability to integrate the activities and resources along the supply chain but also depends on the capability to identify and exploit those critical assets that encourage the development of relationships between port actors and the development of interdependencies between supply chains.

the port competitiveness depends on the capability of the Port Authority in identifying and managing the critical assets and the interdependencies among port actors in order to generate the value for clients.
the development of port competitiveness is a process that requires the definition of a new role of port actors in supply chains and the definition of new relationships between them.
